data.title: Alphabet stock rises 4% as Anthropic IPO boosts investor optimism
data.description:
Alphabet shares GOOGL rose nearly 4% in premarket trading on Thursday as investors welcomed the planned stock market debut of Anthropic, the developer of the Claude artificial intelligence models.

The Google parent’s Class A shares climbed 3.95% to $293.60 before the opening bell.

The move offered some relief after a difficult six months for the stock, which has fallen 31% since reaching a record high of just under $409 on May 18.

Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO), alongside Google’s latest AI product launch, helped improve sentiment towards Alphabet.

However, the company continues to face questions about its AI spending and the performance of its investments outside its core search business.

Anthropic IPO puts Alphabet’s investment in focus

Anthropic is targeting a valuation of $1.5 trillion after setting its IPO price at $83 a share on Wednesday.

The listing could deliver a substantial gain in the value of Alphabet’s investment.

Google is expected to own 1.8 billion Anthropic shares following the IPO and a concurrent private stock sale.

At the IPO price of $83, the holding would be worth approximately $149 billion.

The relationship between the two companies also extends beyond their equity investment.

Anthropic relies on Google's tensor processing unit (TPU) chips to train its Claude large language models.

The IPO has therefore drawn attention to Alphabet's financial exposure to one of the leading companies in the AI industry.

The value of its stake could become an important part of the investment case as investors assess the potential returns from its AI-related businesses and holdings.

However, the investment also exposes Alphabet to fluctuations in the value of Anthropic shares once they begin trading.

SpaceX paper losses highlight investment risks

Alphabet's investment portfolio also presents risks, as demonstrated by the impact of its SpaceX holding on third-quarter earnings.

The company owns approximately 550 million SpaceX shares. During the September quarter, the estimated value of those shares fell from around $171 to $151.

Applied across Alphabet's holdings, the $20 decline translates into an estimated $11 billion reduction in value before taxes.

The adjustment was an accounting requirement reflecting the investment's value at the end of the quarter.

It did not mean Alphabet had sold its SpaceX shares or paid out $11 billion in cash.

The decline in SpaceX shares contributed to Alphabet reporting net income of $26.17 billion, down 25% from a year earlier.

SpaceX shares are currently trading around $143, even below the levels from the third-quarter results, meaning the value of the investment would be even lower.

The contrast between the potential value of Alphabet's Anthropic investment and the recent losses associated with SpaceX highlights the opportunities and risks of its holdings in private technology companies.

Gemini 4 Neon adds to Google's AI push

Alphabet also announced a new AI coding agent, Gemini 4 Neon, late Wednesday.

The model ranked third in Artificial Analysis's ranking of AI models, behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra.

The launch provides another indication of Google's efforts to compete in the increasingly crowded AI market.

The company has been expanding its AI products and infrastructure as competition intensifies among major technology firms.

However, investors have become increasingly concerned about the amount Alphabet is spending on its AI buildout.

These concerns have weighed on the stock, particularly as questions remain about the impact of AI on Google's traditional search business.

data.title: How many investors will rush to buy Anthropic stock? What the numbers say
data.description:
Anthropic starts trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT, after raising $81.3 billion at $83 a share in the largest IPO on record.

The obvious question is how many people around the world will try to buy in. There is no official number, and none of the brokers selling the shares has yet published how many customers applied.

What does exist is a set of hard clues: the size of the order book, how much retail investors asked for and got, and how many people have accounts at the brokers offering access.

What the order book shows?

Orders had reached close to seven times the shares on offer by Sunday, according to Bloomberg, which cited people familiar with the matter.

The book closed on Tuesday. Reuters had reported a six-times book after the roadshow's first three days. That compares with about four times for SpaceX's $75 billion listing in June.

One person told Bloomberg the only comparable book was Snowflake's in 2020, and its shares more than doubled on day one. Demand let Anthropic raise its price above the $70 to $78 range and sell 980 million shares rather than the 825 million first planned, the final prospectus shows.

A multiple of seven sounds modest next to smaller hot deals: Arm's 2023 book was about ten times covered, and Reddit's up to five times. But on a deal this size, even six or seven times cover implies orders worth several hundred billion dollars.

Who could buy at the IPO price?

This IPO was unusually open to individuals. In the US, Anthropic offered shares through Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, SoFi, E*Trade and TradePMR. Its help centre lists retail offers in 14 other countries, through brokers including AJ Bell, Hargreaves Lansdown, eToro and Revolut in the UK, Trade Republic and Scalable Capital in Europe, CommSec in Australia, Wealthsimple in Canada and Rakuten in Japan.

The final prospectus says retail investors received "less than 20%" of the shares, which means fewer than 196 million shares, worth less than $16.3bn at the IPO price.

The UK gives the clearest picture. RetailBook, which ran the UK offer, said on Thursday that 3,614,976 shares, worth about $300m, went to UK investors.

Applications up to $2,822 were filled in full, and about 63% of applicants got everything they asked for. Orders came to close to $1bn, Bloomberg reported, meaning the offer was about three times covered. Investors across the EU, Norway and Switzerland received about 9.7 million shares, worth roughly $801m.

How big is the crowd?

The pool of possible buyers runs to tens of millions. Schwab alone had 40.4 million active brokerage accounts at the end of October, Robinhood 28.7 million funded customers at the end of September, and eToro 4.39 million funded accounts. Many people hold more than one account, so those figures cannot simply be added together.

The closest guide to how many will actually act is SpaceX. Robinhood said all 855,424 customers who requested SpaceX shares through its IPO Access service received some, Bloomberg reported. In Australia, CommSec received more than 28,000 applications.

The record for individual participation still belongs to Saudi Aramco, which drew about 4.9 million individual subscribers in 2019, in a retail offer open only to investors in Saudi Arabia and the Gulf.

India shows that interest reaches well beyond the offer countries. Indians could not apply, but they can buy listed shares under the $250,000-a-year Liberalised Remittance Scheme. Some Indian platforms have seen nearly three times their usual interest this week, Moneycontrol reported, and INDmoney is taking pre-orders.

Vanda Research expects about $250 million of net retail buying on Thursday, more than double SpaceX's record of $118m. Even so, that would be only about 0.3% of the money Anthropic raised. Institutions, not individuals, will set the price.

What history says about day one

Big listings have rarely flopped on day one, but it has happened. Facebook closed just 0.6% above its $38 offer price in 2012 and then fell for months. Alibaba gained 38% in 2014, Arm 25% in 2023, Reddit 48% in 2024 and SpaceX 19% in June.

Early signs point higher for Anthropic. At 13:13 GMT, the Trade.xyz perpetual contract on Hyperliquid was trading at $104.22, about 26% above the IPO price.

Quotes from IG implied a valuation of $1.35 trillion, more than 24% above the IPO price, Bloomberg reported. Polymarket traders put the chance of a close above $83 at about 97%.

What buyers should know

The stock will not trade at 14:30 GMT, when the Nasdaq opens. It first goes through an opening auction, and big IPOs often take hours to open. Market orders placed beforehand can fill well above the last indication. INDmoney's pre-orders, for example, carry a price limit for this reason.

Pre-IPO perpetuals are crypto derivatives with no claim on Anthropic shares. BingX, for instance, renamed and rescaled its Anthropic perpetual this week, and it remains margined in USDT.

Most existing shareholders are locked up for 180 days, the prospectus shows, and the $26bn of shares bought by AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC are restricted securities, although they are not covered by the lock-up. The 980 million shares sold in the IPO are about 7.4% of all shares outstanding, so the free float is thin. Thin floats tend to make prices swing more.

data.title: Kalshi halts Trump 'mention' markets after CFTC opens false certification case
data.description:
Kalshi has halted trading in a set of contracts that let users bet on words President Donald Trump will say, after the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) opened proceedings over whether the exchange falsely certified them.

The order, published on the CFTC's website and dated November 13 according to Cointelegraph and Finance Magnates, stays the listing of the contracts "effective immediately" while the proceeding runs.

It covers the "What nicknames will Trump say before 2027?" market and Kalshi's TRUMPSAY series of contracts on words the president will use.

Kalshi paused the markets, including one on what Trump would say in November, at the end of last week and confirmed the move on Tuesday, CNBC reported.

Why the CFTC acted

The order says Kalshi self-certified the TRUMPSAY series on February 20, 2025, under Commission Regulation 40.2, which lets a designated contract market list a product on its own certificate of compliance without prior CFTC approval.

The contracts are binary and cash-settled, with a $1.00 notional value, according to the order.

On September 22, the CFTC's Division of Market Oversight issued a staff advisory, CFTC Letter No. 26-27, saying contracts settled on whether an individual mentions certain words may be viewed as "presumptively readily susceptible to manipulation". It said exchanges should expect to make a "heightened showing" before listing them.

The order says Kalshi listed the nicknames contract, which has traded since October 1, roughly a week after that advisory, without amending its 2025 certification or filing a new one. A July 29 amendment changed only the rules on multi-word phrases.

"Given the available supporting evidence, including that Kalshi has not attempted to establish that the Contracts are non-manipulable with respect to the Staff Advisory's guidance, the Commission presumptively believes the certification is false," the order states.

The order "makes no final determination as to whether the contracts comply with the Act", and it does not decide whether any presidential mention market can meet the manipulation standard.

Kalshi complies, but disagrees

Kalshi spokesperson Dani Lever said the company is complying with the order, CNBC reported.

Kalshi chief executive Tarek Mansour was blunter at the Axios BFD event on Tuesday. "We disagree with this decision," he said, according to Axios, arguing that "what the president does say moves markets".

CFTC spokesperson Brooke Nethercott told CNBC: "The CFTC stayed the certification of these contracts because they may be susceptible to manipulation, which is consistent with the staff advisory the CFTC put out two months ago."

Kalshi had already stopped listing many mention markets at the regulator's request, including all sports-related ones, Reuters reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. The same person said mention markets had previously generated $90 million a month in trading volume. Invezz could not independently verify that figure.

A test for self-certification

The contracts were already under scrutiny. In an August settlement, the CFTC imposed a three-year trading ban and a penalty of more than $172,000 on a White House teleprompter operator who traded Trump-related mention markets on Kalshi, CNBC reported.

The case matters beyond Kalshi, because event contracts increasingly reach retail traders through brokers and crypto platforms. Last week a Louisiana state judge temporarily barred firms including Kalshi, Robinhood and Coinbase from offering event contracts in the state, an order the CFTC is challenging in federal court. Readers can compare two of those platforms in our Robinhood review and Coinbase review.

CoinDesk said it was unclear whether the CFTC had sent similar orders to other exchanges it regulates.

Kalshi must file a written answer with the Secretary of the Commission by December 11. The CFTC will then decide whether the certification was false and what further action, if any, is warranted.

data.title: Oil price today: Brent holds on Hormuz mine strikes as Goldman sees 2027 decline
data.description:
Oil prices barely moved on Thursday despite Iran's claim that two supertankers had struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, as traders weighed immediate shipping threats against growing evidence that global crude supplies are recovering.

January Brent futures were down 0.34% at $91.64 a barrel at noon in London, according to delayed ICE prices on TradingView. January West Texas Intermediate slipped 0.30% to $82.06.

The muted response comes as Goldman Sachs forecasts a supply surplus next year, suggesting the market is becoming less sensitive to disruption in one of the world's most important oil corridors.

What happened to oil prices today?

Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said two supertankers carrying more than 4 million barrels of crude had caught fire after striking mines while using an unauthorised route through the strait. It alleged the vessels were accompanied by US aircraft.

Neither the ships nor the circumstances were independently identified. The claims, published by Iran's Mehr News Agency, remain unverified.

Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a projectile hit a tanker's engine room near Khasab, Oman, on Wednesday. The crew was safe, although the extent of the damage remained unclear.

The International Energy Agency warned in its World Energy Outlook, released Thursday, that the Hormuz disruption is the largest energy-supply shock on record. It estimates cumulative losses of 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic metres of gas.

Yet mounting disruptions have not produced a comparable surge in benchmark crude prices.

Why is oil barely moving?

Daan Struyven, Goldman Sachs' head of oil research, attributed the market's resilience to Gulf exporters finding alternative routes, including pipelines, escorted voyages and ship-to-ship transfers.

Higher production outside the Gulf, particularly in Brazil, and weaker demand in China have also softened the impact.

Marine-data company Kpler estimated that crude shipments through Hormuz were running at about 8.5 million barrels a day in November through Monday. Including pipelines and other routes, Middle Eastern exports reached around 15 million barrels daily.

That remains far below prewar levels, but it helps explain why threats to individual tankers no longer automatically imply a collapse in worldwide supply.

Pressure is also coming from the US. Energy Information Administration data showed commercial crude stocks rising 3.4 million barrels last week to 417.8 million, a second consecutive build.

Goldman's $78 forecast points to a different oil market

Goldman expects Brent to average $88 in 2027 and drop towards $78 by early December that year, assuming no major escalation damages oil infrastructure.

The bank estimates the market shifted into surplus in October as Gulf crude exports rebounded, and forecasts an excess of 2 million barrels a day next year.

It also expects an additional 3.8 million barrels a day of bypass pipeline capacity over the coming year.

IEA executive director Fatih Birol cautioned that the crisis would leave deeper scars the longer it persists, notwithstanding the resilience of energy producers and consumers.

The next test comes when OPEC+ ministers meet on 29 November to consider 2027 production policy.

For investors comparing the best commodity trading platforms, the distinction between a bearish longer-term forecast and the potential for sudden geopolitical price spikes remains important.

data.title: OpenAI faces fresh legal trouble as Arizona opens criminal probe over rogue agents
data.description:
OpenAI is facing mounting legal scrutiny in the United States as Arizona launched a criminal investigation into the ChatGPT maker over concerns that rogue AI agents may have infiltrated banks.

Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes announced the investigation on Wednesday, saying her office was examining whether AI agents had accessed financial institutions and violated state laws.

OpenAI and some other AI labs have been sued, with Mayes declining ​to identify the other companies her office was investigating.

The development comes just days after California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that the company developed and tested advanced AI models without adequate safeguards.

Arizona investigates rogue AI agents

Arizona's probe centers on the apparent infiltration of banks by autonomous AI agents capable of accessing computer systems and potentially interacting with financial accounts.

"The state of Arizona is very worried about this, and we are looking at it from multiple angles," Mayes told reporters at a press conference in Chicago.

The attorney general said her office had contacted banks operating in Arizona as part of the inquiry.

The investigation does not necessarily mean criminal charges will follow. However, it does highlight growing concerns within the banking industry about allowing third-party AI agents to access customer accounts and conduct transactions.

California AG sues OpenAI

The investigation by Arizona comes after a lawsuit filed by California Attorney General Rob Bonta on November 16.

The lawsuit concerns an incident involving OpenAI's experimental AI agents that allegedly escaped their designated testing environment and carried out a cyberattack on Hugging Face, an open-source AI hosting platform, in July.

According to California's complaint, hundreds of autonomous agents coordinated their activities over more than two days, exploiting vulnerabilities and accessing Hugging Face systems.

The state alleges that the incident reflected inadequate safeguards during OpenAI's model testing.

“The Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability — and this was only one of 80 known incidents,” Bonta said in a statement.

The lawsuit accuses OpenAI of creating a public nuisance and violating California's Unfair Competition Law. It seeks court-ordered changes to the company's safety practices and other penalties.

OpenAI has said it investigated the Hugging Face incident with outside cybersecurity experts, strengthened safeguards and published technical findings.

The company has also introduced a framework for reporting unexpected or misaligned AI behavior.

The latest developments come amid wider legal challenges against OpenAI and other AI labs.

In October, eight states including Arizona filed separate lawsuits alleging that ChatGPT's design and marketing exposed children and vulnerable users to potential harm.

The lawsuits raised concerns about manipulative chatbot interactions, dangerous advice and inadequate safeguards for minors.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield also filed a lawsuit on November 17 seeking $2.035 billion in damages, alleging that OpenAI misrepresented ChatGPT's safety and endangered young users.

data.title: Anthropic IPO: this analyst says ANT stock a buy, sees over 80% upside
data.description:
Needham has initiated coverage of Anthropic with a Buy rating and a $150 price target, signalling substantial upside potential for the artificial intelligence company ahead of its record-breaking stock market debut on Nasdaq on Thursday.

The price target from analyst Scott Berg implies an upside of around 80.7% from Anthropic's IPO price of $83 per share.

The company priced its shares above the initial range of $70 to $78 as investor demand supported a larger offering.

"Growth opportunities like ANT rarely come along but we think history puts ANT in the same dominant bucket as fellow tech titans AMZN, GOOG, and MSFT," Berg said.

Needham sees strong growth and margin potential

Berg described Anthropic as the leading vendor in a rapidly expanding AI market, which he believes could eventually account for 10% of the current $56 trillion labour market.

He said the company's economies of scale and premium brand positioning could give it an advantage in an increasingly competitive industry.

Anthropic could invest tens of billions of dollars annually in model training while maintaining strong profitability, according to the analyst.

Needham expects Anthropic to deliver annual growth of more than 150% in fiscal 2027.

It also sees the company achieving operating margins above 35%, supported by gross margins exceeding 90% and an efficient go-to-market strategy.

Those projections represent a substantial improvement from Anthropic's current financial performance.

The company reported a gross margin of 22% over the last 12 months and remains unprofitable, with negative earnings per share.

Needham's $150 price target values Anthropic at 18 times estimated fiscal 2027 revenue or 81 times free cash flow.

Anthropic raises $81.3 billion in record IPO

Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in its stock market debut after increasing the size of its offering, valuing the Claude chatbot developer at approximately $1.5 trillion.

The IPO eclipsed the previous record set by Elon Musk's SpaceX in June.

Including a further $26 billion being raised through a private placement of shares, the total deal size reached $107.3 billion, according to filings.

The scale of the offering marks a major milestone for the AI industry, which has attracted enormous investor interest despite concerns about the sustainability of technology spending and the ability of companies to generate returns from their investments.

Anthropic shares were trading around 20% higher in over-the-counter grey market activity, brokerages IG Markets and CMC Markets said, according to Reuters.

Other analysts also bullish on Anthropic

Needham is not the only firm taking a positive view of Anthropic's prospects.

Earlier this week, New Street Research initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $105 price target.

Analyst Pierre Ferragu described the offering as a “generational IPO”, arguing that artificial intelligence could represent a structural shift in corporate spending over several decades.

He compared the potential expansion of AI with the adoption of cloud computing, which captured around 30% of incremental IT spending between 2010 and 2025.

AI could spread twice as quickly across an addressable market ten times larger, Ferragu said.

His forecasts suggest AI could account for nearly 7% of knowledge-work spending by 2030, while attracting around 25% of incremental spending through 2040.

At a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion, Anthropic trades at around 8.5 times next year's sales, Ferragu said.

He argued that this multiple is closer to those of Microsoft and Alphabet than the higher valuations assigned to companies such as Palantir, Cloudflare and Snowflake.

In an interview with CNBC, Ferragu said the valuation structure offered some downside protection given the company's expected sales growth.

"A year from now, having it at $105 or above feels like a reasonable bet," he said, adding that Anthropic did not need to meet the most aggressive sales forecasts circulating among bankers and underwriters to justify a strong valuation.

However, Anthropic still faces questions about whether it can sustain its growth as competition across the AI industry intensifies.

data.title: Anthropic IPO opens the door: 4 tech companies that may go public
data.description:
The upcoming Anthropic IPO has already been highly successful as the company has raised over $80 billion from investors. ANT stock is already up by over 20% in the grey market, and the surge may continue, at least in the near term. As a result, this IPO, which is happening during a bear market for AI companies, may open the door for more listings.

OpenAI may go public after the Anthropic IPO

The most obvious company that will likely go public after Anthropic is OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT and the pioneer in the AI space. The company will likely take the cues from Anthropic and launch its IPO.

OpenAI recently raised $11 billion from investors at a $1.25 trillion valuation. It was seeking $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. 

After Anthropic raised over $80 billion, there is a possibility that OpenAI will seek to raise substantial sums of money.

The challenge, however, is that the company’s business is facing substantial headwinds. Its growth has slowed amid the rising competition from companies like Anthropic, Google, and Grok. It is also competing with Chinese companies like Moonshot, Alibaba, and Z.ai.

Anduril plans to go public in 2 years

Palmer Luckey’s Anduril is another company that is watched closely among investors. It has emerged as one of the fastest-growing companies in the world. Also, it has become a disruptor in the defense industry. For example, it is creating a missile interceptor that will cost much less than the Patriot.

Anduril Industries is valued at $124 billion after raising $11.95 billion, making it one of the biggest private companies in the world. Some of its largest investors are Founders Fund, Andressen Horowitz, and Thrive Capital. Anduril has hinted that it will go public in the next two years.

READ MORE: 1789 Capital is raising $3 billion: here are companies in its portfolio

Databricks

Databricks is a top technology company that aims to disrupt Oracle, the biggest database firm in the world. It provides a one platform focusing on data, analytics, and artificial intelligence (AI). 

Databricks has raised about $20 billion from investors like Coatue, Blackstone, T.Rowe Price, Sixth Street, and Goldman Sachs. The fundraising has brought its valuation to about $218 billion. 

The company has remained muted on when it will go public. However, estimates are that it will go public either in 2027 or in 2028. 

Stripe

Stripe is another top company to watch. Started in 2011, the company has become one of the biggest private companies in the world with a valuation of $205 billion after raising over $8.7 billion. According to Forbes, Patrick and John Collinson have a net worth of over $9.3 billion each.

Stripe has always been named as one of the top companies that will go public. However, its officials have remained mute on when the company will go public. 

A key challenge for Stripe is that many fintech companies have struggled in public markets. PayPal stock has dropped by over 81% from its all-time high. Other fintech companies like Block, Shift4 Payments, and Fiserv have dropped by over 50%.

Some of the other top companies that may go public are firms like Kalshi, Perplexity AI, Polymarket, Rippling, and Ramp. Nscale, a top British company that provides neocloud services, has already filed to go public. 

Still, a lot could change, especially if Anthropic’s IPO behaves like other recent companies like SpaceX, Circle Internet Group, and Gemini Space Station, there is a likelihood that many of these firms hold back for a while. Also, they will go public if the stock market drops.

data.title: Bitcoin price could plunge below $60,000 as ETF selling intensifies
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC) struggled to regain momentum on Thursday, trading around $63,750 after falling toward $62,000 on Wednesday as institutional selling and tighter monetary policy expectations weighed on investor confidence.

The cryptocurrency remains under pressure following the release of the Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes, which suggested that policymakers remain concerned about inflation and could support additional interest rate increases.

Meanwhile, US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) continue to experience withdrawals, raising concerns that institutional investors may be reducing their exposure as prices decline.

Hawkish Federal Reserve minutes add pressure to Bitcoin

Bitcoin is down 1% in the last 24 hours, dropping below $64,000. This latest decline coincided with the release of minutes from the Federal Reserve's October monetary policy meeting on Wednesday.

The minutes showed that most policymakers supported leaving interest rates unchanged during the October meeting, although several remained open to additional tightening.

Some officials expressed concern that persistent inflation could require a more restrictive monetary policy stance.

The discussions also indicated that a larger interest rate increase in December could be considered if incoming economic data showed that inflationary pressures were worsening.

The minutes also highlighted concerns about financial risks associated with the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence-related financing.

According to the meeting summary, policymakers observed that AI-related debt had grown significantly, with some financing occurring through complex and relatively opaque structures.

Following the release, BTC declined toward $62,000 on Wednesday before recovering modestly.

Bitcoin ETF outflows reach $306 million as institutional demand weakens

Institutional demand for Bitcoin continues to deteriorate as spot ETFs record another round of withdrawals. According to SoSoValue, US spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced approximately $306.42 million in net outflows on Wednesday.

The withdrawals marked the second consecutive session of negative flows this week, following more than $1 billion in outflows during the previous week.

Persistent ETF withdrawals suggest that investors remain cautious about increasing cryptocurrency exposure amid the recent market downturn.

If the negative flow trend continues, Bitcoin could face additional pressure near important technical support levels. A return to consistent inflows would provide stronger evidence that institutional sentiment is beginning to improve.

Despite the bearish market conditions, on-chain data suggests that Bitcoin may find support near its current trading range.

According to a CryptoQuant report published Tuesday, a significant concentration of long-term holder spending activity occurred between $62,000 and $65,000.

The analysis examined the 30-day sum of long-term holder spending, excluding exchange-related transactions, alongside the prices at which those transactions occurred during 2026.

The highest concentration appeared within the $62,000–$65,000 region. CryptoQuant suggested that the concentration could reflect an important cost-basis area for investors.

Bitcoin remains below major moving averages as bears dominate

Bitcoin's technical outlook remains weak despite its modest recovery from Wednesday's lows. BTC trades around $63,750 on Thursday, significantly below its major daily Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

The 50-day EMA stands near $75,238, while the 200-day EMA is positioned around $75,591. Meanwhile, the 100-day EMA sits at approximately $75,730.

These moving averages form a concentrated resistance zone between $75,238 and $75,730. Trading below all three indicators suggests that the broader trend remains bearish across multiple timeframes.

Momentum indicators reinforce this outlook. The daily Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) remains deeply negative, with the MACD line below its signal line and both positioned beneath zero.

This indicates that bearish momentum continues to dominate. Meanwhile, the Relative Strength Index stands near 25, placing Bitcoin in oversold territory.

An RSI reading below 30 generally suggests that selling pressure has become unusually strong relative to recent buying activity.

Bitcoin's immediate outlook depends on whether buyers can defend the support region between $62,000 and $65,000.

The first important downside reference stands near $62,029, followed by the lower boundary of the broader support structure around $61,300.

A sustained breakdown below $61,300 would weaken the near-term technical outlook and increase the risk of a decline toward $60,100.

If selling pressure intensifies further, the $57,803 cycle low could become the next significant downside target.

On the upside, Bitcoin would need to establish stronger buying demand before challenging higher resistance levels.

$69,400 is the initial recovery target if institutional selling begins to ease. A sustained breakout above this level could open the door to $72,700.

Beyond these targets, Bitcoin faces substantial resistance at its major daily moving averages between $75,238 and $75,730.

A decisive recovery above this cluster would provide stronger evidence that the broader bearish trend is beginning to weaken.

Further resistance stands near $85,000, although this level remains distant under current market conditions.

For now, Bitcoin's near-term outlook remains bearish while ETF withdrawals persist and BTC trades below its major moving averages.

data.title: Did Trump discuss Jensen Huang controversy with Xi? Here's what he said
data.description:
US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said he briefly referred to the controversy surrounding former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang during conversations with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Trump made these remarks in a Fox News interview aired amid the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.

The trade truce between the US and China has been threatened amid the controversy around Nvidia and Huang.

US authorities believe that Alice Huang, who was reportedly involved in a romantic relationship with the former Nvidia boss, was a Chinese intelligence asset.

Beijing denies the allegations as US authorities continue to investigate the matter.

What Trump told Jinping

Trump's latest visit to China assumed added significance in the backdrop of the controversy regarding Huang, who had been a prominent opponent of restrictions on chip sales to China.

When asked if Trump had talked to Jinping about Huang, the US President said he touched upon the matter briefly.

He said the pair spoke throughout a dinner the previous evening and that any mention of Huang was limited.

“I might have referred to it just briefly because it’s such a tragedy. It’s a tragedy. He’s such a brilliant man,” Trump said.

He added that he had not heard claims that the Chinese businesswoman linked to Huang was a spy.

Asked if the affair put national security under threat, Trump said, "I haven't heard that."

The remarks came as Nvidia continues to navigate the fallout from Huang’s resignation last week.

Trump has repeatedly backed Huang, even saying he would not mind seeing the co-founder reinstated in his role as CEO.

The exchange between Trump and his Chinese counterpart occurred ahead of a formal bilateral meeting between the two leaders on the sidelines of the APEC gathering, their third encounter this year.

Trump also highlighted what he called strong personal ties with Xi.

US tightens chip exports

Just days before the summit, the US Commerce Department issued new rules aimed at closing loopholes that allowed Chinese firms to access advanced AI chips remotely or through third countries.

The measures impose licensing requirements on shipments to nations including Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil, and place additional controls on overseas data centers supplying significant computing power to Chinese entities.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun criticized the move as economic coercion that departs from previous consensus.

​Beijing said that it ​hoped ⁠the US would return to ​the "correct track" ​of ⁠resolving differences through consultation and ⁠cooperation. It also warned of countermeasures if the new rules are enforced.

Nvidia to stop chip sales to China

On its earnings call this week, Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress said the company is no longer shipping licensed Hopper-generation data-center products, including the H200, to China.

Nvidia recorded $2.4 billion in such sales in the most recent quarter, but Kress stated that future guidance excludes sales in China.

The halt comes despite earlier US approvals for limited licensed shipments.

Meanwhile, Nvidia’s board has also made clear it does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO, even as the former boss himself remains open to returning.

data.title: Nasdaq futures jump 560 points: 5 things to know before Wall Street opens
data.description:
US stock futures climbed on Thursday as Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering revived enthusiasm for artificial intelligence shares after five consecutive declines in the S&P 500.

Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.06%, or 560 points, while S&P 500 contracts gained 1.12% and Dow futures advanced 0.71%.

The rally followed Wednesday's uneven session, when Nvidia fell despite upbeat earnings and investors digested hawkish Federal Reserve minutes.

Anthropic's Nasdaq debut will test appetite for richly valued technology companies.

Walmart's results, fresh labour-market data and the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI provide other reasons for investors to watch Thursday's opening bell.

5 things to know before Wall Street opens

1. Anthropic's $81 billion IPO tests the AI trade

The Claude developer priced 980 million shares at $83 each, above its marketed $70–$78 range, valuing the company at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

Trading is expected to begin Thursday on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, although the first trade may come later.

The offering helped lift European semiconductor shares even as investors questioned the economics of AI infrastructure.

2. Fed minutes keep a December hike in focus

Minutes of the October meeting showed almost all officials expected further tightening if the economy developed as forecast. Some also considered whether inflation might require a larger increase.

Markets assigned roughly 92% odds to a quarter-point December hike and an 8% chance of a half-point move.

Higher borrowing costs threaten equities despite Thursday's rally. Initial jobless claims, expected at 198,000, and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey are due at 8:30 am ET.

3. Walmart earnings test consumers before the holidays

The retailer is scheduled to release fiscal third-quarter results at 7 am ET, with a conference call an hour later.

Analysts tracked by S&P Global's Visible Alpha expect about $187.3 billion in revenue and earnings of $0.64 a share.

Investors will focus on grocery demand, online sales, margins and whether shoppers are trading down to cheaper goods.

Guidance may indicate whether households can withstand inflation and borrowing costs. Alibaba and PDD Holdings also reported on Thursday, providing a parallel view of Chinese consumers.

4. Asian tech stocks tumble despite stronger Nvidia results

Taiwan's Taiex fell about 4.4%, signalling that enthusiasm for Anthropic had not erased concerns about chip valuations.

Nvidia ended Wednesday down 2.9% even after reporting $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue and forecasting around $130 billion for the next quarter.

Its interim management faces questions about margins, export controls and the cost of supplying increasingly powerful AI systems. Europe showed the opposite early reaction, with ASML and other technology-linked shares gaining.

5. Take-Two faces a high-stakes GTA VI launch

Rockstar Games is releasing Grand Theft Auto VI on Thursday, giving Take-Two Interactive a rare consumer-entertainment catalyst amid the macroeconomic and AI headlines.

Take-Two shares rallied on Wednesday as early reviews strengthened sales expectations. Wells Fargo analysts raised their estimate for units sold in the publisher's fiscal year to 65 million from 35 million and lifted their bookings forecast to $9.76 billion.

That exceeds Take-Two's earlier $8 billion–$8.2 billion guidance. Sales momentum could also influence expectations for console makers and the wider gaming industry.
